# Setting Up Data

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as stats
import os

# --- SETUP (Same as before) ---
os.chdir(r'C:\Users\leanh\Documents\GitHub\Debris-Removal-Optimization')
script_directory = os.path.dirname(__file__)
Lee_County_path = os.path.join(script_directory, 'input', 'LEE COUNTY')
load_path = os.path.join(Lee_County_path, 'Lee_Co_FOIA_Request_Load_Location_with_CYD_12.21.23.csv')
df = pd.read_csv(load_path)

# # --- MOCK DATA FOR DEMONSTRATION (Replace this with your actual file loading) ---
# # I'm creating a dummy DF to simulate your 2022-2025 timeline
# dates = pd.date_range(start='2022-10-01', end='2023-05-01', freq='D')
# # Create a "spike" early on, then very low values for years
# vol_early = np.random.normal(1000, 200, 180) # High volume first 6 months
# vol_late = np.random.uniform(0, 50, len(dates)-180) # Low volume rest of time
# cyd_data = np.concatenate([vol_early, vol_late])
# # ensure no negative
# cyd_data = np.abs(cyd_data) 
# df = pd.DataFrame({'Disposal Date': dates, 'CYD': cyd_data})
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Ensure date format is correct and sorted
df['Disposal Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Disposal Date'])
df = df.sort_values('Disposal Date')

# =========================================================
# PART 1: Raw Data Histogram (Daily Bins over 3 Years)
# =========================================================
plt.figure(figsize=(15, 6)) # Wide figure for long timeline

# Calculate exact number of days for bins
min_date = mdates.date2num(df['Disposal Date'].min())
max_date = mdates.date2num(df['Disposal Date'].max())
days_span = int(max_date - min_date) + 1

date_nums = mdates.date2num(df['Disposal Date'])

# Plot Histogram with bins = total number of days
plt.hist(date_nums, bins=days_span, weights=df['CYD'], 
         color='skyblue', edgecolor='none', label='Daily Volume')

plt.title('Raw Debris Timeline (2022 - 2025)')
plt.ylabel('Cubic Yards (CYD)')
plt.xlabel('Date')

# X-Axis Formatting for Long Durations
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y-%m')) # Show Year-Month
# plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.MonthLocator(interval=3)) # Label every 3 months
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=2)) # Every 2 weeks
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# =========================================================
# PART 2: Determine "Baseline Time" (Cut off the Long Tail)
# =========================================================
# We use Cumulative Volume to find when the "real work" was done.
df['cumsum_cyd'] = df['CYD'].cumsum()
total_volume = df['CYD'].sum()

# 95% is the standard engineering threshold for "Substantial Completion"
cutoff_percent = 0.95 
cutoff_threshold = total_volume * cutoff_percent

# Find the exact date we hit 95%
cutoff_row = df[df['cumsum_cyd'] >= cutoff_threshold].iloc[0]
cutoff_date = cutoff_row['Disposal Date']

print(f"Total Volume: {total_volume:,.0f} CYD")
print(f"95% Completion Date: {cutoff_date.date()}")
print(f"This is your 'Baseline Completion Time'.")

# Filter data to only include the "High Activity" phase
df_filtered = df[df['Disposal Date'] <= cutoff_date].copy()

# =========================================================
# PART 3: Fit Distribution to the Active Phase
# =========================================================
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Recalculate bins for just the short period
filt_min = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'].min())
filt_max = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'].max())
filt_span = int(filt_max - filt_min) + 1

filtered_date_nums = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'])

# 1. Plot Histogram (Density=True for curve fitting)
plt.hist(filtered_date_nums, bins=filt_span, weights=df_filtered['CYD'], 
         density=True, alpha=0.5, color='green', label='Active Phase Data')

# 2. Fit the Distribution
# We calculate weighted stats to find the center of mass of the debris
weighted_mean = np.average(filtered_date_nums, weights=df_filtered['CYD'])
weighted_var = np.average((filtered_date_nums - weighted_mean)**2, weights=df_filtered['CYD'])
weighted_std = np.sqrt(weighted_var)

# Generate the curve
x_line = np.linspace(filt_min, filt_max, 200)
pdf = stats.norm.pdf(x_line, weighted_mean, weighted_std)

plt.plot(x_line, pdf, 'k-', linewidth=2, label='Normal Dist (modeled baseline)')

# 3. Add visuals to show the "Baseline Time"
# Draw a vertical line where the user "should" have finished according to the curve
# (Usually defined as Mean + 2 Sigma for ~97% confidence)
theoretical_end = weighted_mean + (2 * weighted_std)
# plt.axvline(theoretical_end, color='red', linestyle='--', label='Theoretical Completion (Mean + 2$\sigma$)')

plt.title(f'Baseline Distribution (Oct 2022 - {cutoff_date.strftime("%b %Y")})')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Density')
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y-%m-%d'))
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=2)) # Every 2 weeks
plt.xticks(rotation=90)
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```















```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.dates as mdates
import numpy as np
import scipy.stats as stats

# Set the current working directory to the project root if necessary
os.chdir(r'C:\Users\leanh\Documents\GitHub\Debris-Removal-Optimization')

# Get the directory where current Python script is located. This makes paths relative to the project's root
script_directory = os.path.dirname(__file__)

# Construct the path to 'input' folder relative to the script. Assumes 'input' folder is in the same (sub-)directory as script
Lee_County_path = os.path.join(script_directory, 'input', 'LEE COUNTY')

# Load debris load locations for entire Lee County
load_path = os.path.join(Lee_County_path, 'Lee_Co_FOIA_Request_Load_Location_with_CYD_12.21.23.csv')
df = pd.read_csv(load_path)

# Ensure date format is correct
df['Disposal Date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['Disposal Date'])
df = df.sort_values('Disposal Date')

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Part 1: Simple Histogram
# ---------------------------------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))

# We convert dates to numbers for plotting
date_nums = mdates.date2num(df['Disposal Date'])

# Plot: weights=df['CYD'] ensures the bar height represents VOLUME, not just truck count
plt.hist(date_nums, bins=50, weights=df['CYD'], color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')

plt.title('Debris Removal Timeline (Raw Data)')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Cubic Yards (CYD)')
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y-%m-%d'))
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Part 2: Remove Outliers (The "95% Complete" Rule)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Calculate cumulative volume to find where the "main work" finished
df['cumsum_cyd'] = df['CYD'].cumsum()
total_volume = df['CYD'].sum()

# Define cutoff (e.g., 95% or 99% of total volume)
cutoff_percent = 0.95 
cutoff_threshold = total_volume * cutoff_percent

# Find the date where we crossed this threshold
cutoff_row = df[df['cumsum_cyd'] >= cutoff_threshold].iloc[0]
cutoff_date = cutoff_row['Disposal Date']

print(f"Baseline Completion Date (95% Volume): {cutoff_date}")

# Create new filtered dataset
df_filtered = df[df['Disposal Date'] <= cutoff_date].copy()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Part 3: Plot Distribution / Fit Curve (Daily Resolution)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6)) # Made figure slightly wider for daily detail

# 1. Calculate the exact number of days to create "Per Day" bins
# We find the min and max date to determine the span
min_date = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'].min())
max_date = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'].max())
days_span = int(max_date - min_date) + 1 # +1 ensures the last day is included

# Get numbers for filtered dates
filtered_date_nums = mdates.date2num(df_filtered['Disposal Date'])

# 2. Plot Histogram with Daily Bins
# bins=days_span ensures 1 bin = 1 day
plt.hist(filtered_date_nums, bins=days_span, weights=df_filtered['CYD'], 
         density=True, alpha=0.6, color='green', label='Observed Data (Daily)')

# 3. Fit Normal Distribution
weighted_mean = np.average(filtered_date_nums, weights=df_filtered['CYD'])
weighted_var = np.average((filtered_date_nums - weighted_mean)**2, weights=df_filtered['CYD'])
weighted_std = np.sqrt(weighted_var)

# Generate the bell curve line
xmin, xmax = plt.xlim()
x = np.linspace(xmin, xmax, 200) # Increased resolution for the line
p = stats.norm.pdf(x, weighted_mean, weighted_std)

plt.plot(x, p, 'k', linewidth=2, label='Normal Distribution Fit')

# 4. Format X-Axis for Daily Visibility
plt.title(f'Baseline Debris Removal Distribution\n(Daily Resolution - Outliers removed after {cutoff_date.date()})')
plt.xlabel('Date')
plt.ylabel('Probability Density (Volume Weighted)')

# Set the formatter to Year-Month-Day
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter('%Y-%m-%d'))

# LOCATOR: This controls how many text labels appear on the X-axis.
# If the period is short (<60 days), show every day:
# plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.DayLocator(interval=1)) 

# If the period is long (>60 days), show every Monday (interval=1) or every 7 days
# This keeps the BARS daily, but prevents the TEXT from overlapping
plt.gca().xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.WeekdayLocator(interval=1)) 

plt.xticks(rotation=90) # Rotate 90 degrees to fit more dates
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```
